2024-12-09-written-in-music-various-arti.kurz: The Dutch review of Ian Rankin’s compilation *Behind the Counter* names Jackie Leven, with ‘Another Man’s Rain’, as one of Rankin’s ‘great heroes’ who naturally could not be missing.
inhalt: The review on Written in Music covers the second volume of Rough Trade’s *Behind the Counter* series, this time compiled by the Scottish crime writer Ian Rankin, known as a notorious record buyer and music lover. The reviewer praises the stylistic range: Joy Division, Magazine, Throbbing Gristle, The Cure, Carmel, Scritti Politti, Simple Minds, Julie Fowlis, Roy Budd and others. That such an album requires laborious rights clearance is obvious.

On Jackie Leven it says: “A song by one of Rankin’s great heroes, Jackie Leven, can of course not be missing: ‘Another Man’s Rain’.” The track sits on side A of the vinyl edition beside Throbbing Gristle, Isobel Campbell, Kath Williams and Roy Budd. The text says nothing more about the song; it merely confirms Rankin’s admiration for Leven, which also gave rise to their joint album *Jackie Leven Said*.

The verdict: a “rich, musically broadly varied and constantly surprising” compilation, a very fine second part of a great series; available for now only from Rough Trade’s own shop. The displayed rating is 4.5; Leven is not rated individually.

2024-12-28-toppermost-doll-by-doll.kurz: Toppermost piece presenting Doll by Doll through ten selected songs, written by a fan who often saw the band and Leven as a solo artist live (short biography at the end: lives near Brighton).
inhalt: Toppermost piece presenting Doll by Doll through ten selected songs, written by a fan who often saw the band and Leven as a solo artist live (short biography at the end: lives near Brighton). He sketches the origin of the band name (E. E. Cummings), the line-up, Leven's earlier history (duo Saint Judas with Colin Soutar around 1969, album “Control” as John St Field) and his literary sources (James Wright, Blake, Rilke, Robert Bly, Anna Akhmatova). Discussed are, among others, “More Than Human” and the B-side “The Fountain Is Red, The Fountain Is White” (presumably inspired by Baudelaire) from “Remember”, “Hell Games”, “Stripshow”, “The Human Face” and “Highland Rain” from “Gypsy Blood”, “Those In Peril” and “Main Travelled Roads” from the third album, and “Lonely Kind of Show” and “So Long Kid” from “Grand Passion”. The author recalls often seeing Leven in the late 1970s with friends at the Warwick Castle pub in Maida Vale – the loudest group at the bar, occasionally brawling. He mentions a German TV recording of “Main Travelled Roads” (1981), the unreleased fifth album “The Last Flick of the Golden Wrench” (possibly identical with “The Robberies of the Rain”, which according to the author came out in 2009) and the tribute concert “Two Tiny Selves” in 2012 at The Castle pub. In Leven's memory he had a memorial bench placed in Soho Square. Tone: affectionate, very personal, a plea for an underrated band. In the comments further witnesses of the time come forward (concerts in Liverpool, Camden Lock, Farnborough, Blandford Forum) and a relative of Jo Shaw.
zitate_kontext: on Leven and friends at the Warwick Castle.

2025-04-24-wikipedia-arz-jackie-leven.kurz: A bot-generated stub from the Egyptian Arabic Wikipedia, fed from Wikidata: Jackie Leven, born 18 June 1950 in Kirkcaldy, died 14 November 2011 of lung cancer. Apart from an infobox the entry contains very little.
inhalt: The article in the Egyptian Arabic Wikipedia consists essentially of an infobox populated from Wikidata. It lists Jackie Leven as a Scottish singer, born on 18 June 1950 in Kirkcaldy and died on 14 November 2011 aged 61, with lung cancer given as the cause of death. It also records British citizenship, guitar and voice as instruments, English as his language, music as his field and a link to the official website. The label is Cooking Vinyl, the genre traditional music.

The entry gives 2011 as the start of his working period. That is an error carried over from Wikidata, where 2011 is wrongly recorded as the “start of work period”, not a statement by the source about Leven’s career; in reality he began in the late 1960s. There is no running text and there are no references; the stub was created in 2020 and last edited by a bot in April 2025.

2025-10-24-the-afterword-from-tom-newlan.kurz: A thread on The Afterword that moves from a Fife novel to Jackie Leven: long passages from Paul Du Noyer's obituary (bars, Rankin, the Ted Heath anecdote) and readers' comments.
inhalt: The thread “From Tom Newlands to Robert Louis Stevenson via Jackie Leven and the Kingdom of Fife” on the British forum The Afterword (24 October 2025, 55 comments) starts with a question about Tom Newlands's debut novel *Only Here, Only Now* and grows into a collection of Scottish writers and musicians. The opening poster, who lives in Stockholm, writes that research on Fife led him to the music of Jackie Leven, born in Kirkcaldy. One commenter calls him “the Late Great Jackie Leven” and says you can't go wrong discovering his musical legacy.

Asked where Leven fits in, the original poster pastes long passages from Paul Du Noyer's obituary. According to it, Leven was born Alan Moffatt in 1950 and grew up in the Pictish region he called the Kingdom of Fife; his parents were English, with Romany and Irish ancestry. He claimed to be the first child ever expelled in Scotland over drugs and to have been a schoolmate of the future Prime Minister Gordon Brown in Kirkcaldy. His real love was bars, which he listed on every album sleeve – especially the haunts of old working men whose lives had lost meaning with the closure of mines, mills and factories (“Poortoun”, 1997, draws on images of Fife). Ian Rankin, also a Fifer, was drawn to this dimension, picturing his detective Rebus consoling himself at night with these songs: “stories about disappointed hard men”.

Leven's own anecdote is quoted too: when Ted Heath visited his school and asked what he wanted to be, he said he would like to be one of those wee men in flat caps standing outside the pubs – Heath laughed, the headmaster did not. Leven's partner Deborah Greenwood explains the image: as a boy he waited outside bars for his father; that was where the men were, where the big mystery would be revealed, “a Congregation of Men”. Other comments recall Rankin's background in Cardenden and a meeting of Leven and Ralph McTell with Gordon Brown at Downing Street. Most of it is second-hand; what is telling is how Leven's self-mythology has settled in the minds of a late audience.
zitate_kontext: Du Noyer on Leven, as quoted in the thread.
Deborah Greenwood on Leven's childhood, as quoted in the thread.

2026-01-04-wikipedia-pl-jackie-leven.kurz: The Polish Wikipedia article is a brief sketch: Leven as a Scottish rock and folk musician, poet and composer, with phases as John St Field, with Doll by Doll and as a solo artist, followed by a discography and videography.
inhalt: The article (version of 4 January 2026) calls Jackie Leven a “Scottish rock and folk musician, poet and composer”, born on 18 June 1950 in Kirkcaldy, Fife, who died on 14 November 2011 “aged 61 after a long battle with cancer”; the infobox lists the pseudonyms John St Field and Sir Vincent Lone, activity from 1971 to 2011 and the label Cooking Vinyl. The biographical section has only a few sentences: he was born into a Roma family, began in the late Sixties as John St Field, recorded the album *Control* in 1973 (released two years later), was from 1977 to 1982 singer, leader and main songwriter of the rock group Doll by Doll, and released his first solo album, *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death*, in 1994. Since then more than twenty records have appeared under his own name or the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone.

Most of the space goes to the discography after AllMusic: *Control* (here “1971”, released only in Spain, reissued by Cooking Vinyl in 1997), four Doll by Doll albums (*Remember* and *Gypsy Blood* in 1979 on Automatic, *Doll By Doll* in 1981 and *Grand Passion* in 1982 on Magnet) and the live album *Revenge of Memory* (2005), then the solo records from *Songs from the Argyll Cycle, Vol. 1* (1994) to *Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man* (2011, with Michael Cosgrave), including the Sir Vincent Lone albums *Songs for Lonely Americans*, *When the Bridegroom Comes* and *Troubadour Heart*, the collaboration with Ian Rankin (*Jackie Leven Said*) and *Elegy for Johnny Cash*. A “videography” lists the DVDs *The Meeting of Remarkable Men* (2005) and *Live at Rockpalast* (2011). The sources cited are Robin Denselow's Guardian obituary and the AllMusic discography.

The text contradicts itself on *Control* (recorded 1973, listed as 1971 in the discography), has Doll by Doll end in 1982 (elsewhere 1983) and lists the fan-club CD *Barefoot Days* among the regular solo albums.

2026-02-18-wikipedia-de-jackie-leven.kurz: The German Wikipedia article gives a compact life story from John St. Field through Doll by Doll, the assault and CORE to the Haunted Year reissues and the alter egos Sir Vincent Lone and Jackie Balfour.
inhalt: The article (here in the version of 18 February 2026) calls Jackie Leven, born in Kirkcaldy on 18 June 1950 and died on 14 November 2011, a British songwriter and folk musician, the “son of an Irishman and a Roma woman”. His career began in the late 1960s under the pseudonym John St. Field, under which he recorded the album *Control* in 1973. Inspired by punk, after a period of travelling he founded Doll by Doll, dated here to 1978; the band were hugely popular live but never made the final breakthrough (citing Edo Reents’s obituary in the FAZ of 15 November 2011). Four albums appeared between 1979 and 1982.

After the band broke up in 1983 Leven began a solo career. While recording his first solo album he was attacked at night in the street and throttled, which left him unable to speak for almost two years; he took drugs and became addicted to heroin. The single ‘Big Tears’, released as ‘Concrete Bulletproof Invisible’, became Melody Maker’s Single of the Week in 1988. He freed himself from addiction through acupuncture and founded the CORE Trust, which advocates a holistic approach to heroin addiction. His solo career proper began in 1994 with *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death*; by his death he had released 15 solo albums and various fan-only material. *Jackie Leven Said* (2005) is a collaboration with the crime novelist Ian Rankin, who also comes from Fife.

The fan society The Haunted Valley received a limited album once a year, usually of live recordings; the series *The Haunted Year* (Winter, Spring, Summer, Autumn) reissued these as double CDs. What sets the article apart from the English version is its paragraph on pseudonyms: as Sir Vincent Lone he released three albums of songs on themes too far removed from his folk image – for example ‘The War Crimes of Ariel Sharon’, which asks about the causes of the former Israeli prime minister’s coldheartedness, and ‘Moscow Train’, a fictional train journey from Berlin to St Petersburg on which he chats to Bob Dylan about the Moscow metro. With his last alter ego, Jackie Balfour, he continued what he had hinted at on live albums such as *For Peace Comes Dropping Slow* and on *Jackie Leven Said*, his talent as a storyteller; the first album, *Chip Pan Fire*, appeared at the end of 2007. His death after serious illness is sourced to Spiegel Online; a role-by-role discography and web links follow.

Some details differ from other sources: the founding year of 1978 and the account of his parentage are reported differently elsewhere, the assault is placed in 1983 (English sources often give 1984), and *Control* appears once as recorded in 1973 and, in the discography, as released in 1975.

2026-03-13-grants-rock-warehaus-jackie-l.kurz: A short YouTube video (56 seconds) from a collectors' channel on Leven's lost falsetto after an attack and his subsequent path to more folk-based solo work.
inhalt: The video “How Jackie Leven from Doll by Doll lost his falsetto — and kept creating” on the channel Grant's Rock Warehaus was published on 13 March 2026 and runs for 56 seconds. Its description is a generic promotional text: it promises the “inspiring story” of the musician from the Scottish rock band Doll by Doll, who faced a significant challenge in his career, the loss of his “iconic” falsetto, and how he adapted and went on to produce “remarkable work” despite the setback, from the early days of Doll by Doll to a solo career blending folk, rock and poetic lyrics.

In the video itself the speaker says, in a short excerpt from a chat stream, that after the Doll by Doll records Leven had his larynx crushed in an attack and never sang falsetto again, but got over his addiction and made around twenty more folk-leaning solo albums. The video is inaccurate and adds little; the speaker also says Leven died about ten years ago (he died in 2011).

2026-05-22-wikipedia-en-jackie-leven.kurz: The English Wikipedia article presents Leven as a Scottish songwriter who found success with Doll by Doll, became addicted to heroin after an assault, co-founded the CORE Trust and restarted at Cooking Vinyl in 1994; Leven’s own quotation explains the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone.
inhalt: The article calls Jackie Leven (18 June 1950 – 14 November 2011) a Scottish songwriter and folk musician, born in Kirkcaldy, Fife, with the birth name Alan Moffatt. His career began in the late 1960s under the pseudonym John St Field; the album *Control*, recorded in 1971, was released only in Spain, in 1973. Doll by Doll, formed in 1977 according to the article, released four albums between 1979 and 1982. After the band split in 1983 Leven began a solo career, but in 1984, while recording his first solo album, he was assaulted in the street and nearly strangled, leaving him unable to speak for almost two years. During this time he became addicted to heroin.

With former Doll by Doll members Joe Shaw and David Macintosh and ex-Sex Pistol Glen Matlock he recorded the single ‘Big Tears’ as Concrete Bulletproof Invisible, a Melody Maker Single of the Week in 1988. He cured himself of addiction, with the help of his wife Carol, through acupuncture and psychic healing; this led to the Core Trust, which favours a holistic approach to heroin addiction. In 1994 his solo career restarted with the mini-album *Songs from the Argyll Cycle* and the album *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death* on Cooking Vinyl, in folk-rock style. Fifteen further albums followed, including *Jackie Leven Said* with Ian Rankin and the multi-instrumentalist Michael Cosgrave, plus limited fan-club live albums via the Haunted Valley fanzine.

Leven himself explains the Sir Vincent Lone pseudonym, introduced in 2006 with *Songs for Lonely Americans*: he noticed he was writing far more songs than he could record, and his boss Martin Goldschmidt said no to more records because it was not 1967 and he was not the Beatles. They agreed he could make records under another name. Later milestones: *When the Bridegroom Comes* (2007, first sold only at gigs, then commercially), *Lovers at the Gun Club* (2008), *Troubadour Heart* (2009), the four Haunted Year double CDs, *Gothic Road* (2010) and, in September 2011, *Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man* with Cosgrave. Leven died on 14 November 2011 aged 61 of cancer; he had been due to play the Green Hotel in Kinross on 18 November. A discography follows, grouped by role (solo, fan-club, singles, DVDs).
Some details differ from other sources, such as the founding year of 1977, the year of the assault and the dating of *Revenge of Memory* to 1977.
zitate_kontext: Leven on the origin of the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone

2026-07-10-ruta-66-sir-ian-rankin-el-pun.kurz: Agudo asks Ian Rankin about the relationship between rock music, his own writing and the character John Rebus.
inhalt: Agudo asks Ian Rankin about the relationship between rock music, his own writing and the character John Rebus. The introduction describes how the Spanish translations, from “Black & Blue” onwards, also made musical discoveries possible. Leven appears expressly as one of the musicians readers became aware of through the novels.

Rankin explains that music is so often central in his books partly because he himself would have liked to be a musician. The mentions in turn made musicians into readers and made personal meetings and joint appearances possible; as an example he names the collaboration with Leven on “Jackie Leven Said”. Asked about this mediating effect, he replies that he is pleased when readers thereby discover Leven, Mogwai or Blue Rose Code.

The conversation also covers punk as encouragement to write, Rankin's earlier band, Van Morrison and instrumental background music while working. It provides no new chronology of the relationship with Leven and names no first Rebus novel with a Leven reference. Its value lies in the reception continuing into 2026: a Spanish rock magazine asks Rankin specifically about Leven's discovery through the crime novels.

2026-07-26-lifo-jackie-leven-astypalaia-.kurz: Long essay by the Greek music critic Fontas Troussas introducing Leven to Greek readers by two routes: music and literature.
inhalt: Long essay by the Greek music critic Fontas Troussas introducing Leven to Greek readers by two routes: music and literature. First the connection with Ian Rankin (shared origin in Fife; Rankin discovered Leven through a record review, “Shining Brother Shining Sister” impressed him), the Crossing Border evening in The Hague in November 2003 and “Jackie Leven Said”; Troussas traces Rebus novel titles back to Leven songs (“Standing in Another Man's Grave” to “Another Man's Rain”, “Saints of the Shadow Bible” to “One Man One Guitar”, “A Heart Full of Headstones” to “Single Father”).

Greece is central: Leven lived on Astypalea in May and September of each year from 1991 to 1997 (about 14 months in all); Troussas translates Leven's booklet text for “Greek Notebook” (Haunted Valley, 1999; 33 pieces, 52:29) at length, including a cave-like house on a mountain top and about 40 hours of Walkman recordings. Later Leven described himself as a resident of Paxos; according to posts by Paxiots he loved Loggos, spent months there and sat on an old iron bench by the sea. After his death Deborah Greenwood had a memorial bench (backrest with a guitar body and strings, plaque) made by a local carpenter and placed at the entrance to the old customs house; in 2021 unknown persons threw it into the sea, it was fished out, repaired and put back. On 23 June 2022 a memorial concert took place in the old school of Loggos, with Greenwood, Jinder, Michael Weston King and the Paxiots Ilias Dendias and Spyros Kavvadas.

A personal section describes how Troussas knew “Control” as a Spanish Movieplay rarity and only learned from the Korean vinyl reissue of 2002 (Merry-Go-Round/Beatball, 500 copies, four-page liner notes) that John St. Field was Leven; he translates Leven's liner note (LSD phase 1971, pseudonym because of problems with the police). Finally, short reviews of “The Haunted Year / Spring” (2009) and “Lovers At The Gun Club” (2008), which he says he had earlier reviewed for the magazine “Jazz & Τζαζ”. Tone: knowledgeable, warm appreciation.
zitate_kontext: Caption/leitmotif: a wandering artist with an eventful life.

2026-08-28-wikipedia-en-doll-by-doll.kurz: The English Wikipedia article outlines Doll by Doll as a London band founded by Leven in 1977 and overlooked by the press, with line-ups, albums, the 1997–98 reunion and the 2007 CD reissues.
inhalt: The English Wikipedia article (version of 28 August 2026) describes Doll by Doll as a British rock band based in London, formed by Jackie Leven in 1977. They came to prominence in the new wave period but were largely ignored by the music press, their emotional, psychedelic-tinged music being judged out of step with other bands of the time. The band took its name from a line in E. E. Cummings's poem “the first of all my dreams”.

The original line-up was Leven (vocals, guitar), Jo Shaw (vocals, guitar), Robin Spreafico (vocals, bass) and David McIntosh (vocals, percussion); it recorded only the album *Remember*, produced by Bill Price. Spreafico was then replaced by Tony Waite, and in that configuration they made *Gypsy Blood* (produced by John Sinclair) and the eponymous third album (produced by Tom Newman). After touring it Leven sacked McIntosh and Waite, who were replaced by Andy Anderson (drums) and John Reid (bass). By the final LP, *Grand Passion*, only Leven remained of the original line-up, joined by Helen Turner and Tom Norden and guests including David Gilmour of Pink Floyd and Mel Collins; Mark Fletcher and Chris Clarke played live. A fifth album, *The Last Flick of the Golden Wrench*, was recorded but never released.

In early 1983 Leven announced that the band – now with Carol Pearett and Gary Thompson – would continue under his name alone, and his solo debut appeared in September of that year. In 1988 Leven, Shaw, McIntosh and ex-Sex Pistol Glen Matlock released the single “Big Tears” as Concrete Bulletproof Invisible, a Melody Maker single of the week. In 1997 Leven, Shaw, McIntosh and Waite reformed for a few live shows; their final appearance was as support to Pere Ubu at the Queen Elizabeth Hall, London, in 1998. In 2005 *Revenge of Memory*, a live recording of the original band which the article says was made at the Sheffield Limits Club in 1977, was released. The four studio albums appeared on CD for the first time in March 2007 on WEA/Rhino. The discography lists *Remember* and *Gypsy Blood* (Automatic, 1979), *Doll by Doll* (Magnet, 1981), *Grand Passion* (Magnet, 1982) and *Revenge of Memory* (Haunted Valley, 2005).

Some of these details are contested: Leven himself dates the band's founding to 1975; Tony Waite's dates are given as 1958–2003 here, other sources say 1953–2002; and the 1977 recording date for *Revenge of Memory* is doubtful, Leven himself giving 1980.
zitate_kontext: Wikipedia on how the music press saw Doll by Doll.
Wikipedia on the unreleased fifth album.

2026-09-14-store-norske-leksikon-jackie-.kurz: The Store norske leksikon portrays Leven concisely as a Scottish song-singer and composer with poetic, personal lyrics, gives the outline of his career and praises his voice, the quality of his albums and his concert storytelling.
inhalt: The signed article by Svein Askheim in the Norwegian national encyclopaedia (subject area song-writing, “visesang”) describes Leven as a Scottish singer, guitarist and composer who wrote poetic and personal lyrics; his music was marked by his Celtic roots, and he performed several times in Norway. The fact box gives his birth name as Alan Moffatt, his birth date as 18 June 1950 (place according to the article: Glenrothes, Fife) and his death as 14 November 2011 (place: Botley, Hampshire).

Under “Career” it says Leven released his first album in 1971 under the name John St Field. From 1978 to 1983 he was vocalist and songwriter of the London band Doll By Doll, which released four pop-rock albums. His solo career began in earnest in 1994 with *The Mystery of Love is Greater Than the Mystery of Death*.

The verdict is consistently appreciative: Leven had a beautiful, strong voice and released many records, all of high quality. He gave memorable solo concerts in which he often spent several minutes between songs telling both humorous and serious stories. Because of his large output, Cooking Vinyl encouraged him to release some albums under the artist name Sir Vincent Lone; he also had exclusive fan-club releases. A selection of albums from 1994 (*The Mystery of Love …*) to 2010 (*Gothic Road*) closes the entry, among them *Night Lilies*, *Shining Brother Shining Sister*, *Jackie Leven Said* (with Ian Rankin), *Elegy for Johnny Cash* and *Lovers at the Gun Club*.

Opening sentence of the encyclopaedia entry.

2026-10-17-wikidata-q432870-jackie-leven.kurz: The Wikidata entry for Jackie Leven (Q432870) lists life dates, membership of Doll by Doll, the label Cooking Vinyl and numerous authority and database identifiers; “lung cancer” appears as cause of death without a source.
inhalt: Item Q432870, created on 5 December 2012, describes Jackie Leven as “Scottish musician, poet (1950–2011)”. The statements: born 18 June 1950 in Kirkcaldy, died 14 November 2011, cause of death lung cancer (natural causes), school Kirkcaldy High School, member of Doll by Doll, record label Cooking Vinyl, website jackieleven.co.uk. The entry links six Wikipedia language editions (English, German, Norwegian, Polish, Egyptian Arabic, Volapük).

Its main function is as a hub to authority records and databases: among them VIAF, ISNI, GND (with further records), the Library of Congress, the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the Czech National Library, MusicBrainz, Discogs (artist ID 140574), Songkick, Rate Your Music, Pitchfork, Deezer, Yandex Music, Muziekweb and Musik-Sammler.de. It also points to three reference works: the Store norske leksikon, Munzinger Pop and Oxford Reference.

Two statements are faulty or unverified: “start of work period: 2011” is wrong, since Leven’s career began around 1971; the error has already migrated into an automatically generated Egyptian Arabic Wikipedia article. The cause of death, lung cancer, carries no source, and other sources dispute the type of cancer (pancreatic, prostate or lung). As birthplace Wikidata gives Kirkcaldy; the Store norske leksikon gives Glenrothes.

2026-12-09-ents24-main-travelled-roads-t.kurz: Announcement of a tribute night for Jackie Leven, “Main Travelled Roads”, on 9 December 2026 at Leytonstone Ex-Servicemen's Club, London: Leven as one of Scottish pop's “nearly men”, with over 300 songs and tall tales.
inhalt: The listings site Ents24 lists “Main Travelled Roads – A Tribute to Jackie Leven” for Wednesday 9 December 2026 at 7.30pm at Leytonstone Ex-Servicemens Club, London. Tickets cost £13.20 including booking fee and are sold through WeGotTickets. The page names no performers; the strapline reads “One of the UK's greatest songwriters remembered”.

The promotional text recalls “the maverick genius of the late great Scottish songwriter and folk musician”. He was “one of Scottish pop's nearly men”: emerging in the febrile post-punk era of the late 1970s with Doll by Doll, “a ferocious, by all accounts even intimidating, live act”, he survived a brutal assault and heroin addiction in the 1980s to become a cult singer-songwriter much loved by critics and loyal fans (including the crime writer Ian Rankin) but, sadly, ignored by the wider world. He died of cancer in 2011 aged 61, leaving more than 300 songs and “a book full (maybe more than one) of tall tales attached to his legend, some of them even true”, taking in everyone from Princess Di to the Dalai Lama. inhalt: Michael Weston King's discography lists his own albums (among them *God Shaped Hole* 1999, *Live…In Dinky Town* 2002, *A Decent Man* 2003, *Absent Friends* 2004, *The Tender Place* 2005 and *Love's A Cover* 2006), compilation contributions and guest appearances on other artists' albums. 2026-searching-for-a-gem-dylan-unrelease.titel: Directory of Bob Dylan's Unreleased Songs (entries "Moscow Train" and "As We Sailed Into Skibbereen")
2026-searching-for-a-gem-dylan-unrelease.kurz: A fan directory of unreleased Dylan songs lists two alleged “co-compositions” with Leven, “As We Sailed Into Skibbereen” and “Moscow Train”, both based on Leven's own account of a train journey with Dylan; the page itself doubts the story.
inhalt: The “Searching For A Gem” directory has two entries, both resting on Leven's account in the Dylan fanzine *The Telegraph* (issue 51). According to it, Leven, former leader of Doll By Doll, met Bob Dylan in a Berlin hotel bar on 5 October 1988 and then travelled with him by train from Berlin to St Petersburg.

“As We Sailed Into Skibbereen”: during the journey Leven says he showed Dylan some song lyrics, and Dylan suggested setting them to the melody of “One Too Many Mornings”. The song appeared, credited to “Jackie Leven/Bob Dylan”, in 1994 on the Cooking Vinyl CD single *I Say A Little Prayer* (FRY CD 036) and later on the album *The Argyle Cycle* (as the page spells it; properly *The Argyll Cycle*, dated 1996). Columbia reportedly forced the single's withdrawal in the UK, though apparently not in Germany. The page points out that Dylan is known from Heylin's day-by-day chronicle to have been in Beverly Hills on 5 October (it writes “1998”, evidently a slip for 1988), and that the fan Dieter Petzold explains Leven is known for “tall tales and leg pulls”, of which this is one.

“Moscow Train”: Leven wrote this second “co-composition”; in his live introduction he claims that Dylan suggested the line “A closed-eyed woman is looking at me on a Moscow train” when describing his experience of the Moscow subway in October 1985. The song is on *Songs For Lonely Americans* (Return To Sender Records, Germany, 2004; Cooking Vinyl, UK, 11 September 2006), which according to the page Leven recorded under the pseudonym “Sir Vincent Lone” for “copyright reasons” (the page's own guess). Dylan is not credited.
zitate_kontext: The entry on Dieter Petzold's view of the Dylan story

undatiert-allmusic-doll-by-doll-biograph.kurz: Jason Ankeny’s brief AllMusic biography presents Doll by Doll as Jackie Leven’s vehicle: formed in 1977, four albums up to *Grand Passion* (1982), an unreleased fifth album and the break-up.
inhalt: This one-paragraph band biography by Jason Ankeny, which appeared on AllMusic and is read here in the identical text on Apple Music’s artist page, describes Doll by Doll as the showcase of the Scottish-born singer-songwriter Jackie Leven, who had previously gigged under the name John St. Field. With the dawn of the new wave, it says, Leven formed the band in 1977, recruiting guitarist Jo Shaw, bassist Robin Spreafico and drummer David McIntosh.

Two years later came the debut LP *Remember*, a collection informed as much by R&B and Celtic influence as by post-punk attitude. With new bassist Tony Waite the group returned later in 1979 with *Gypsy Blood*, followed two years later by a self-titled LP and the “minor hit ‘Carita’” (meaning the single “Caritas”). After *Grand Passion* (1982) the band recorded a fifth album that was never released; the group disbanded, and Leven soon mounted a solo career. The text calls the band London-based and dates its formation to 1977, whereas Leven himself places it earlier.
zitate_kontext: Jason Ankeny on the formation of Doll by Doll

undatiert-allmusic-jackie-leven-biograph.medium: AllMusic (TiVo), mirrored on Qobuz and others
undatiert-allmusic-jackie-leven-biograph.kurz: Thom Jurek’s long AllMusic biography follows Leven’s life from childhood in Fife through Doll by Doll, the assault and the heroin years to the late albums and his cancer, and calls *Forbidden Songs of the Dying West* arguably his masterpiece.
inhalt: At around 2,000 words, Thom Jurek’s is by far the longest database biography of Leven. He portrays him as a singer, storyteller, traveller and fingerstyle guitarist with a baritone, and then follows the life chronologically: birth as Alan Moffatt in Kirkcaldy to English parents of Irish and Roma descent, a school friendship with Gordon Brown, Leven’s claim to have been the first Scottish pupil expelled for drugs, an anecdote about Ted Heath, poetry from Burns to Mandelstam. He learns guitar from his mother’s records (Elvis, Lightnin’ Hopkins) and singing from “Rescue Me”; sectarian gangs follow, a first marriage at 16 and a son, years of wandering in Ireland, Berlin and Madrid, *Control* in Spain and a squat at the South Bank Centre.

He meets Jo Shaw in a folk club in Dorset; Doll by Doll record for Automatic and Magnet, John Peel plays “Main Travelled Roads” and “Caritas”, and the band is thrown off tours with Devo and Hawkwind. Then come *Grand Passion*, a Charisma single in 1983 and the assault after a mixing session in which his throat is slashed; the album *The Robberies of the Rain* is left unfinished. Heroin, recovery and the CORE Trust with Carol Wolf (patron Diana, later Prince Charles), Robert Bly via the Dalai Lama’s bodyguard, the men’s movement, Concrete Bulletproof Invisible, the deal with Goldschmidt in late 1993 and the albums up to *Wayside Shrines* follow, with Haunted Valley, Germany and Norway as his biggest markets, Deborah Greenwood and the cottage in Hampshire, Ian Rankin, the pseudonyms, giving up alcohol in 2010, the cancer diagnosis in 2011 and posthumous releases up to *Straight Outta Caledonia* (2021).

Greenwood reports that Leven would often vanish for days while writing and sleep in fields; a concert at the Green Hotel in Kinross was said to have been booked for the evening of his death. The tone is affectionate. Jurek calls *Forbidden Songs of the Dying West* “arguably Leven’s masterpiece”. Errors in the text: it gives 11 rather than 14 November 2011 as the date of death, attributes “Clay Jug” to Hafiz instead of Kabir, and dates some albums differently (*Oh What a Blow …* 2006, *Shining Brother, Shining Sister* 2002).

undatiert-allmusic-the-wanderer.kurz: On AllMusic Thom Jurek praises the fan-club live album *The Wanderer* (1999): superbly recorded solo shows in which Leven combines guitar, whistling, singing and storytelling, plus Doll by Doll guests as true bonuses.
inhalt: The review (by Thom Jurek, undated; AllMusic lists the album as August 1999) places the album in the series of live records Leven issued through his fan club, the Haunted Valley, to document his “exciting” solo gigs between studio albums for Cooking Vinyl. *The Wanderer* is usually available only from his website, to the faithful of the fan club; here it is packaged as a bonus disc in a Cooking Vinyl box that includes *Forbidden Songs of the Dying West*, *Fairytales for Hard Men* and the 1971 album *Control*. In addition to the box's “deep price”, the Cooking Vinyl edition of *The Wanderer* has three extra tracks. The material comes from solo gigs in England, Scotland, Wales, Norway, Poland and Australia and is “impeccably” recorded. (The album page lists, among others, Bergen, the Borderline in London, the Queen Elizabeth Hall, a radio concert in Poznań, St Columba's Cathedral in Oban and Sydney as recording locations.)

The set opens with a moving rendition of “Your Winter Days”, a stark meditation on loss and regret, and follows with a “gorgeous” medley of “Newfoundland Blues”, “Some Ancient Misty Morning”, “Working Alone” and “Sex Tourist”. Here one gets a taste of Leven's ability to play guitar, whistle, sing, play harmonica and put across a series of tales “as living moments from the center of his heart”; there is no overt sentimentality, just emotional power. The real bonuses are a complete reunion of Doll by Doll – Jurek calls it Leven's “famed and simultaneously vaunted and hated post-punk band” of the late Seventies – on “I Can't Afford to Care Anymore”, and Doll by Doll's former rhythm guitarist Joe Shaw on “When a Man Dies”. Overall the set is recorded better than the two previous volumes and, with the other three records in a handsome box, “pretty much pays for itself”.

A bracketed note says Haunted Valley reissued the CD in 2000 with bonus material: a full-on band version of “Donna Karan” with Doll by Doll and the vocalist Deborah Greenwood, the “crazy poetic rant” “So My Soul Can Sing”, and a “beautiful but loopy” folk tune called “Mary Jane's Dog”. Jurek's statements on the box and on *Control* are not independently verified.
zitate_kontext: Thom Jurek on Leven's solo shows

undatiert-apple-music-jackie-leven-artis.autor: Apple Music (text abridged from AllMusic/Thom Jurek)
undatiert-apple-music-jackie-leven-artis.kurz: The short Apple Music biography calls Leven a Scottish singer-songwriter, storyteller and fingerstyle guitarist blending Celtic folk, blues, rock, doo-wop, soul and country, and mentions Doll by Doll, his solo albums, David Thomas and Ian Rankin.
inhalt: The artist biography on Apple Music (UK store) sums Leven up in a single paragraph: a Scottish singer/songwriter, storyteller, traveller and raconteur, a formidable fingerstyle guitarist with a mellifluous baritone voice. Stylistically his work crisscrossed and combined Celtic folk, blues, rock, doo-wop, soul, girl-group pop and country.

In the late 1970s he co-founded the "art punk" outfit Doll by Doll and issued four acclaimed albums, including 1979's *Gypsy Blood*. His "26-album" solo career began with 1994's *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death* and included 1995's *Forbidden Songs of the Dying West* and 1997's *Fairytales for Hard Men*. He collaborated with Pere Ubu's David Thomas on three albums, including 2001's *Creatures of Light & Darkness*. *Jackie Leven Said*, a live collaboration with author Ian Rankin, appeared in 2005. *Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man* was released in September 2011, two months before Leven died of cancer aged 61.

The page also lists popular tracks (among them "The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ", "Some Ancient Misty Morning", "Gothic Road", "Poortoun", "Single Father" and "Snow in Central Park") and the albums available on the service, such as *Gothic Road* (2010), the four *Haunted Year* double albums (2009), *Lovers at the Gun Club* (2008) and *Oh What a Blow That Phantom Dealt Me* (2007). The text is a condensed version of the AllMusic biography; the 1995 date for *Forbidden Songs* differs from the usual dating, and the number of solo albums is the blurb's own count.

undatiert-deezer-jackie-leven-artist-bio.autor: Music Story (supplier of the Deezer bio)
undatiert-deezer-jackie-leven-artist-bio.kurz: Deezer's artist biography sums up Leven's career in a few sentences, from *Control* (1971, as John St Field) through Doll by Doll and Cooking Vinyl to his death from cancer on 14 November 2011.
inhalt: The short biography on Deezer calls Leven a singer-songwriter born in Scotland on 18 June 1950. It says he first recorded *Control* in 1971 as John St Field and formed Doll by Doll in 1977, who released four albums until 1983. After a violent assault that left him mute for two years, he returned to recording in 1984 and issued the single “Big Tears” with Glen Matlock in 1988. In 1994 he signed to Cooking Vinyl and released *The Mystery of Love Is Greater than the Mystery of Death*, followed by numerous albums, including the Sir Vincent Lone releases *Songs For Lonely Americans* (2006) and *Troubadour Heart* (2009).

It also mentions the collaboration with Ian Rankin on *Jackie Leven Said* (dated 2005 here; the show premiered in January 2004) and with Michael Cosgrave on *Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man* (2011). It ends with the sentence that Leven died of cancer on 14 November 2011. The page also counts 30 albums and about 525 fans. The text is in the present tense and was evidently written during his lifetime, with the ending added.

undatiert-discogs-cbi-und-ubudoll.titel: C.B.I. (Concrete Bulletproof Invisible) and Ubudoll (Discogs group profiles)
undatiert-discogs-cbi-und-ubudoll.kurz: Discogs lists Concrete Bulletproof Invisible as one of Glen Matlock’s post-Pistols projects with ex-Doll by Doll members Leven, Shaw and McIntosh (only release “Big Tears”), and Ubudoll as the acoustic duo of David Thomas and Leven around 1999 (only release *Lore*, 2023).
inhalt: The Discogs entry for C.B.I. describes the group as one of Glen Matlock’s post-Sex Pistols projects. The other members were all former Doll by Doll men: vocalist Jackie Leven, guitarist Joe Shaw and drummer Dave McIntosh. On record they were augmented by James Hallawell on keyboards and Mike Spencer on harp. The band played in places as diverse as Scandinavia and Oban but never toured properly.

“Big Tears” was the only release; the American version of the 12-inch on Dimension Records (1988) also included “Love Kills”, a track the band recorded for the film *Sid & Nancy*, which was not used. The discography lists the master of “Big Tears” as 1987 and the release as 1988.

The entry for Ubudoll describes the collaboration between David Thomas of Pere Ubu and Jackie Leven, “two very distinctive voices in the rock business”. They did very few shows together around 1999, offering an original acoustic set of songs from Leven’s solo repertoire and Pere Ubu tracks completely rearranged. Two fan pages on David Thomas are linked. The only release listed is *Lore* (2023), a recording of a concert on 17 May 1999 at the Hôtel du Nord in Paris, chosen by Thomas himself and distributed through Pere Ubu’s Bandcamp page (listed as a FLAC download).

undatiert-discogs-doll-by-doll-bandprofi.kurz: The Discogs profile describes Doll by Doll as a London rock band founded by Jackie Leven in 1975, with Leven, Jo Shaw, Tony Waite, David McIntosh and Robin Spreafico as members.
inhalt: The Discogs band profile presents Doll by Doll as a London rock band founded by Jackie Leven in 1975 and well known in the new-wave era. Listed as members are Jackie Leven, who is also credited as ‘Alan Moffatt’, Jo Shaw, Tony Waite, David McIntosh and Robin Spreafico. According to the profile the band split after the third, self-titled album, which was recorded in 1980 but long held back for contractual reasons. The fourth album was then Leven with Helen Turner and session musicians.

The catalogue lists 21 entries, 13 of them as main artist. The member profiles themselves are sparse – ‘Guitarist.’, ‘Bassist.’, ‘UK rock drummer.’ – except that for the guitarist Jo Shaw a user contribution gives the real name John Anthony Daragaville Culshaw and a former membership of the Pretty Things. These are unreferenced user-generated claims. The founding year of 1975 matches Leven’s own accounts.

undatiert-discogs-jackie-leven-kuenstler.kurz: Discogs artist profile: a short biography (18 June 1950 – 14 November 2011) plus aliases, name variants and groups, including Sir Vincent Lone, John St. Field, Saint Judas and Ubudoll.
inhalt: Discogs profile no. 140574 carries a three-sentence biography: Jackie Leven was a Scottish songwriter and folk musician (18 June 1950 – 14 November 2011). He started his career as a folk musician in the late 1960s, was then singer in the new wave band Doll by Doll, and later recorded as a solo artist, releasing more than twenty albums under his own name or under the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone. The entry's data quality is marked “Needs Vote”, that is, not yet finally checked.

More revealing are the links to other names and projects. Listed aliases are Sir Vincent Lone, Alan Moffatt, Jackie Balfour and John St. Field; name variations include “J. Leven”, “Jackie Levan”, “Jackie Levin” and “Levin”. Groups recorded are Doll By Doll, Jackie Leven & The Stornoway Girls, Jackie Leven & The Celtic Soulmen, C.B.I., Saint Judas, Small World Orchestra and Ubudoll. Behind these names stand collaborators such as Michael Cosgrave and David Thomas. The database lists over 200 entries under the name, nearly 60 of them as main artist.
zitate_kontext: From the short biography in the Discogs profile

undatiert-discogs-john-st-field-und-pseu.kurz: Discogs lists John St. Field, Sir Vincent Lone, Jackie Balfour and Alan Moffatt as alias profiles linked to each other and to Jackie Leven; under John St. Field it lists the album Control (Movieplay, Spain).
inhalt: The Discogs profile "John St. Field" (no. 2897689) gives "Jackie Leven" as the real name and lists "Alan Moffatt", "Jackie Balfour", "Jackie Leven" and "Sir Vincent Lone" as other names. There is no biographical text. The discography consists of a single album, *Control* (Movieplay, catalogue number S-32.738, Spain), dated there to 1975, plus credits (vocals, instruments, writing and arrangement, production) and ten linked videos. The archived page of February 2021 also showed 41 marketplace listings and several pending submissions.

The other alias profiles are cross-linked: "Sir Vincent Lone" (no. 1741578) with three main releases, "Jackie Balfour" (no. 2435395) with "Chip Pan Fire", and "Alan Moffatt" (no. 1833275), who is listed as a member of Doll by Doll, apparently for credits under his birth name. Discogs's date of 1975 for *Control* differs from the 1971 recording date given for it elsewhere, for example in the four-CD box *Great Songs from Eternal Bars*; the spread of years reflects the unclear release history of the Spanish edition.

undatiert-dnb-katalog-tontraeger-jackie-.titel: [Catalogue of the German National Library: sound recordings by and with Jackie Leven]
undatiert-dnb-katalog-tontraeger-jackie-.kurz: The catalogue of the German National Library lists about forty recordings by or with Leven. They chiefly document his German distribution: Teldec in 1983, Public Propaganda (Hamburg) in the Cooking Vinyl years, Normal Records in 2004, MIG Music from 2011.
inhalt: The German National Library’s catalogue (Deutsches Musikarchiv) holds about forty records on Jackie Leven, mostly legal-deposit copies of German editions. They show who brought Leven’s music out in Germany. *Grand Passion* was released by Teldec in Hamburg in 1983. The Cooking Vinyl albums of 1994 to 2001 – from *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death* and *The Right to Remain Silent* through *Forbidden Songs of the Dying West*, *Fairy Tales for Hard Men* and *Night Lilies* to *Creatures of Light & Darkness* – appeared through the Hamburg licensee Public Propaganda, partly distributed by Indigo. The same goes for singles and EPs such as *I Say A Little Prayer*, *Leven’s Lament*, *Some Ancient Misty Morning*, *Universal Blue* and *Control* (1997).

Further entries: *Songs for Lonely Americans* appeared in 2004 on Normal Records in Bonn, with the performer given as “Vincent Lone”. Leven is listed as a contributor to David Thomas’s album *Act 1. Jack & the General* (1999, Public Propaganda). There are also two samplers (Vol. 1 from 1996 and another) and single-track records for songs from the albums of 2000 and 2001. The most recent entries concern the MIG Music (Hannover) releases: the DVD *Live at Rockpalast* (2011, recorded in 2004 at the Harmonie in Bonn with Michael Cosgrave and Kevin Foster) and *Live or Die – live in Bremen, 1999 & 2004* (2024), partly also recorded as online resources in 2025 and 2026.

undatiert-el-lokal-zuerich-unser-freund-.kurz: The Zurich venue El Lokal remembers Leven in an obituary: repeated visits, his humour, a cancelled last concert; he is said to have died of cancer in Southampton on 14 November 2011.
inhalt: On the continuously extended memorial page “Insel Olymp” of the Zurich venue El Lokal, in a section carrying no date, a short obituary by the promoter is headed “Our friend Jackie Leven has gone” (“Unser Freund Jackie Leven ist gegangen”). Leven had been to the venue “many times”. Unfortunately he had to cancel his last concert on “our island”: the Scottish singer and “wonderful storyteller” was admitted to hospital as an emergency. He died, the text says, on the evening of Monday 14 November 2011, at eight o’clock, in Southampton; he had been suffering from cancer. The exact place and time are the promoter’s statement, with no source disclosed.

They will never forget “this loving bear of a man”, the promoter writes, nor the “funny pranks” he often played on them: someone who “sparkled with wit, humour and zest for life” will never drop by again. The obituary closes with a quotation from Leven, in German translation, about two kinds of storyteller: there are spiritual storytellers and soulful ones; he hopes he belongs to the latter, whose stories reach into the earth, have sap and are nourishing, rather than striving upward towards heaven and God like the spiritual ones.
zitate_kontext: The promoter El Lokal in its obituary
Jackie Leven, quoted in German translation at the end of the obituary

undatiert-glitterhouse-mailorder-jackie-.titel: [Glitterhouse Mailorder: Jackie Leven artist page with catalogue texts]
undatiert-glitterhouse-mailorder-jackie-.kurz: The mail-order firm Glitterhouse lists six Leven releases with sleeve-style texts, including two MIG live releases from 2024, the expanded reissue of *The Mystery of Love* and the tribute *The Wanderer*.
inhalt: The artist page of the German mail-order firm Glitterhouse lists six Jackie Leven items, each with a catalogue text on its product page. The 4-CD set *Live Or Die (Live in Bremen 1999 & 2004)* (MIG, 26 April 2024) contains two concerts recorded by the broadcaster: solo in 1999 at the Bremen music club “Moments”, and in 2004 in Radio Bremen's Sendesaal with his long-time friend and companion Michael Cosgrave on keyboards. The track list shows Leven's spoken passages are listed as titles in their own right (“Jackie Talking About Football”, “Alvis Green”, “Glen Matlock is drinking…”). The accompanying text summarises his biography: born in Kirkcaldy in 1950 “the son of an Irishman and a Romani woman” (Leven's own account of his parentage, taken over by the catalogue), starting out as John St. Field with the album *Control* (1973), founding Doll by Doll in London in 1978, whose four albums did not reach the expected sales, their split in 1983, his breakthrough as a solo artist only eleven years later with *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death*, three albums as Sir Vincent Lone with songs too far outside his folk image, and his death in 2011 aged 61.

The CD+DVD *Live At Rockpalast 2004 w/ Michael Cosgrave* (MIG, 27 September 2024) was recorded at the “Harmonie” in Bonn and features highlights of *Shining Brother, Shining Sister* as well as “Call Mother A Lonely Field”, the “first Jackie Leven hit”. The text calls Leven “perhaps Scotland's greatest singer/songwriter”, a master of the mature melody who blurs the line between pure folk and sophisticated pop, with melancholy, biographical songs and an ironic humour shown in his concert stories; it gives 14 November 2011 as the date of his death.

For the expanded reissue of *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death* (Cooking Vinyl, 12 November 2021; 2-CD and coloured double LP) the shop reproduces an English review that appears to come from AllMusic: an album that intrigues and puzzles on first listen, with no premeditated format, ranging from Celtic mysticism and Bacharach-David crooning to Big Country-ish epics, loosely linked by poetry fragments intoned by Robert Bly, with Mike Scott of the Waterboys guesting and Leven's deep, reverb-laden vocals recalling Scott Walker. The tribute *The Wanderer: A Tribute To Jackie Leven* (Cooking Vinyl, 22 October 2021) offers 22 newly recorded tracks, including by Eliza Carthy, Ralph McTell, Boo Hewerdine, Tom Robinson, James Yorkston, Johnny Dowd and Ian Rankin; each contributor wrote booklet notes on their connection with Leven, and the proceeds go to the Westminster Drug Project, which continues the work of Leven's CORE Trust.
zitate_kontext: English text reproduced for the reissue of *The Mystery of Love*.

undatiert-god-save-the-sex-pistols-concr.kurz: Fan-site article by Jim Henderson on Glen Matlock's post-Pistols band Concrete Bulletproof Invisible with Jackie Leven, Joe Shaw and Dave McIntosh: how it formed, the single of 1988, and a song recorded for “Sid & Nancy”.
inhalt: On Phil Singleton's fan site “God Save The Sex Pistols”, Jim Henderson describes Concrete Bulletproof Invisible (CBI) as one of Glen Matlock's numerous post-Pistols projects. The other members were all former Doll by Doll men: vocalist Jackie Leven, guitarist Joe Shaw and drummer Dave McIntosh. The explanation for the band is unglamorous: they all lived close to each other and drank in the same local. They first played together at a benefit at the Camden Palace for the dependants of the late Gary Holton, and encouraging chance remarks from Robbie Coltrane, who also took part, motivated the four to take themselves seriously as a new unit.

The only UK release came on RadioActive in 1988: “Big Tears” (written by Matlock) / “Braid on My Shoulder” (by Leven), with “Good Thing” by Joe Shaw added on the 12-inch. James Hallawell played keyboards and Mike Spencer harmonica; Matlock and Dave Goodman produced. The band played places as diverse as Scandinavia and Oban in Scotland but “never toured properly”. The US 12-inch on Dimension Records included an extra track, “Love Kills”, recorded for the film “Sid & Nancy” but not used. Leven said it was too well played, and told Wavelength magazine that there might be a bit more hanging around from that time, “but not much”. The back sleeve of the US pressing gave Matlock's then home address as a contact.

Afterwards McIntosh worked with Matlock again (he was the original drummer in Matlock's 1990s group The Mavericks), Hallawell appeared on The Philistines album and Matlock's solo album, and Chelsea's Gene October covered “Big Tears”. Leven, the page says, released several solo albums in the 1990s, including *Night Lilies* on Cooking Vinyl in 1998. The text has errors worth knowing: it has Doll by Doll splitting in “1985” after four albums (they ended in 1982) and calls Leven's assault merely an “accident” after which he could not sing for two years. Its value lies in the CBI detail, which is hard to find elsewhere.
zitate_kontext: Henderson on how the band came about.

undatiert-gristlepop-jackie-leven-night-.kurz: A US webzine review of *Night Lilies*: the writer is no folk fan and hears “Celtic Lounge Lizard”, but praises the gritty, personal and tender lyrics, above all the title song.
inhalt: This short album review from an American webzine opens by noting that Leven is hugely popular in Scandinavia, Germany and Scotland but has failed to catch on in the United States. As a prelude the writer strings together four compliments from other reviews, among them “a stirring soul singer and poet of raw intensity” and one of the great white soul voices of our time, and quotes the line that Leven is “in danger of becoming a national living treasure”.

His own verdict is deliberately detached. Folk is “not exactly my cup of tea (or scones)”, so he consults a folk-loving friend, who hears bits of Del Amitri mixed with “an angry John Gorka in a kilt”. The Scottish influences are plainly audible throughout, from the uillean pipes in “Burning the Box of Beautiful Things” to the violins, mandolins and whistles across the eleven tracks. To the reviewer, though, the music sounds swanky, more “Celtic Lounge Lizard” than “Celtic Soul”, and he finds the whip-cracking in “Live or Die” gratuitous.

What brings him back are the lyrics. Leven’s greatest strength, he says, is his writing – gritty, poignant, masculine, painfully personal and at times tender. He calls the title track a touching portrait of how the sense of smell floods us with vivid memories, and sees each song as a miniature study in loss and quiet desperation, for which the acoustic setting fits quite well. His conclusion: anyone interested in folk should check this artist out and see why “those pesky Scandinavians” love him to pieces.

The reviewer’s folk-loving friend on the sound

undatiert-imdb-jackie-leven-nm5250531.kurz: IMDb lists just one credit for Jackie Leven: “Self” in the video release *Jackie Leven Live: The Meeting of Remarkable Men* (2004).
inhalt: The person entry nm5250531 contains no biography and no further details, only an invitation to contribute a bio, trivia and more. The only credit is “Himself” in *Jackie Leven Live: The Meeting of Remarkable Men* (Video, 2004), a title that is also linked to Ian Rankin. No other film, television or soundtrack credits, for example for concert recordings or uses of songs, are listed. The version of the page in the Internet Archive from 2017 likewise shows only this single entry.

undatiert-kieler-nachrichten-der-kauz-im.kurz: The Kieler Nachrichten finds Leven at Kiel’s KulturForum a “gruff troubadour” and “gentle rough diamond”: songs alternate with anecdotes, *Gothic Road* is at the centre, and there are no encores.
inhalt: This concert review, preserved in a weblog repost from May 2010, describes Leven through a string of contrasts: gruff troubadour, gentle rough diamond, hulking tenderfoot, hard-drinking philosopher, world-travelling true Scot. Most of the well-attended house at Kiel’s KulturForum knew him already.

The text recounts one of his stories: a woman called Deborah is expecting money from Stuttgart and, at a Western Union branch in Southampton, has to answer the security question set by the sender. The clerk asks, “Who am I?”, and Deborah answers: “You’re an arsehole.” “That is correct,” says the clerk, and pays out. In the songs, by contrast, the humour often gives way to a delicate, at times dark, hopeless and clear-sighted melancholy that, at its best, pulls the listener “into the bottomless” with inescapable weight – the review names “Elegy For Johnny Cash” and “Kings Of The Infinite Space”.

Michael Cosgrave accompanies on keyboards, “unobtrusively and elegantly”, which gives the folk-rooted songs, seasoned with soul, pop and country, more breadth. Embedded in the “thicket of anecdotes”, the critic finds them rounder, more intense and more direct than on record. The roughly two-hour concert centres on the new album *Gothic Road* – “Last Of The Bad Men”, “John Paul Getty’s Silver Cadillac” and “Song For Bass Guitar And Death” are named. As usual there were no encores: they are “all wrong and plastic”, and nobody, after the guests have left the house, flings the door open and yells “Encore!” after them. A funny, clever fellow, concludes the review – though the delighted audience would have liked one anyway.
zitate_kontext: The critic on the balance of humour and melancholy in Leven’s songs
The critic on the songs in combination with the stories
The critic on Leven’s refusal to play encores

undatiert-musicbrainz-jackie-leven-und-d.kurz: The MusicBrainz entries list Jackie Leven (Kirkcaldy, 18 June 1950 – 14 November 2011) with his aliases, and Doll by Doll (London, 1975–1983) with dated memberships; they carry no explanatory text.
inhalt: MusicBrainz is an open music database. Its entry for Jackie Leven describes him as a person from the United Kingdom, born on 18 June 1950 in Kirkcaldy and died on 14 November 2011. Recorded name variants are “Jacky Leven”, “Jakie Leven” and “Sir Vincent Lone”. Sir Vincent Lone, John St. Field and Jackie Balfour are linked as separate artist identities of his. He is listed as an original member of Doll by Doll (from 1975, guitar and lead vocals) and as a member of UbuDoll. There are also links to Discogs, streaming services, MySpace, Songkick, his official homepage and authority files (VIAF, Wikidata).

The Doll by Doll entry describes the group as a London band active from 1975 to 1983. Memberships are dated: Robin Spreafico (bass, vocals) 1975–1979, Jo Shaw (guitar, keyboard, lead vocals) 1975–1981, David Macintosh (drums, vocals) 1975–1983 and Tony Waite (bass) 1979–1983, plus Leven himself. Sir Vincent Lone has an entry of his own, marked as a Leven alias. None of the three entries has an explanatory free-text annotation.
The 1975 founding date matches Leven’s own account, whereas English Wikipedia gives 1977; Jo Shaw’s departure in 1981 is not confirmed elsewhere.

undatiert-normdaten-gnd-loc-viaf-jackie-.kurz: The authority records of the German National Library (GND), the Library of Congress and VIAF list Jackie Leven with dates (18 June 1950, Kirkcaldy - 14 November 2011), a link to Doll by Doll and three separate pseudonym records.
inhalt: The Integrated Authority File (GND) of the German National Library lists Leven under number 134444035 as a differentiated person, "Leven, Jackie", with the dates 18 June 1950 to 14 November 2011. The record was created as early as 4 April 1998, which shows that the library was already cataloguing Leven recordings in the Cooking Vinyl era, and last changed on 14 July 2022. It links to the corporate body Doll by Doll (GND 10276696-4, also created in 1998) and, since 9 February 2022, to three separate pseudonym records: "Balfour, Jackie", "Lone, Vincent" and "St. Field, John", with a note that further titles may be found under his real name or the other pseudonyms.

The Library of Congress authority record (LCCN no2009121313) was created from a "Cooking Vinyl America sampler" and takes its dates from the Guardian website of 15 November 2011 ("b. 18 June 1950, Kirkcaldy, Fife; d. 14 Nov. 2011; singer-songwriter"). The Virtual International Authority File (VIAF 43052884) merges these records with those of the French and Czech national libraries and Canadiana. Two ISNI numbers are linked across Wikidata and the GND, probably a duplicate. The records are thin in content but useful as a basis for library catalogue searches.

undatiert-nts-radio-jackie-leven-artist-.kurz: The artist page of London's NTS radio lists Leven's songs on shows such as “Plz Make It Ruins” (first 28 February 2018) and carries a Wikipedia-based biography covering pseudonyms, the CORE Trust and his death.
inhalt: The artist page of the London internet radio station NTS says that Jackie Leven has been played on NTS in shows including “Plz Make It Ruins w/ Vegyn”, first featured on 28 February 2018; the songs played include “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” and “Soft Lowland Tongue”. It shows Leven reaching younger, experimentally minded radio listeners years after his death.

Below is a Wikipedia-based biography: a Scottish songwriter and folk musician (18 June 1950 – 14 November 2011) who began as a folk musician in the late 1960s, first found success with new wave band Doll by Doll and later released more than twenty albums under his own name. As John St. Field he recorded *Control* (the page says 1971; other sources say 1973), and as Sir Vincent Lone *Songs for Lonely Americans* (2006), *When The Bridegroom Comes (Songs for Women)* (2007) and *Troubadour Heart* (2008). Since 1994 he released eleven albums, including the duet with Ian Rankin featuring the exclusive short story “Jackie Leven Said”. In the 1980s there were two singles, “Love Is Shining Down On Me” and “Uptown”; then in 1983 he was the victim of an unprovoked attack, nearly strangled, lost his voice for a year and became addicted to heroin. After recovering he set up the CORE Trust, a charity taking a holistic approach to drug addiction, whose patrons included Princess Diana.

He returned to music in the early 1990s with live shows, followed in 1994 by *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death*. Since then his songs have followed a dark, gloomy theme; Leven described them as “saying shit happens” and then helping people deal with it. On his albums he read poems and stories (James Wright, Rainer Maria Rilke) and collaborated with poets and authors including Robert Bly and Ian Rankin, as well as David Thomas of Pere Ubu. He died on Monday 14 November 2011 after suffering from prostate cancer.

From the biography on the page.

undatiert-official-charts-the-mystery-of.kurz: Official Charts records *The Mystery of Love Is Greater* for 11 August 2022 in four sub-charts: No. 34 on the Scottish Albums, 19 on the Record Store Chart, 40 on the Independent Albums and 12 on the Independent Album Breakers.
inhalt: The chart history from the Official Charts Company lists Jackie Leven's album (Cooking Vinyl, catalogue number COOKCD064) with exactly one week on chart, that of 11 August 2022. It reached No. 34 on the Official Scottish Albums Chart, No. 19 on the Official Record Store Chart, No. 40 on the Official Independent Albums Chart and No. 12 on the Official Independent Album Breakers Chart. The database lists no further weeks, no No. 1 or top-10 placing and no entry on the main UK albums chart; it provides only the placings, with no text about the album.

undatiert-pitchfork-jackie-leven-night-l.kurz: A mocking pan of the US edition of *Night Lilies* (score 5.1): Michael Sandlin concedes an earthy atmosphere but accuses Leven of overwritten, pseudo-literary lyrics and samey mid-tempo songs, comparing him to John Denver and Bono.
inhalt: Michael Sandlin reviews the US edition of *Night Lilies* (Thirsty Ear) for Pitchfork and awards it 5.1. He opens sarcastically with Leven wanting to be seen as a mere reed in the swamp, but concedes a loamy, mossy earthiness reminiscent of late-eighties 4AD echo-chamber sound, only less reverb-dependent: a soft, muted pall over every song, “like a light, creamy fog hanging over a Scottish moor”.

Then comes the criticism. The contemporary, Scottish-flavoured folk-pop does smack of sophistication, but the lyrics suffer from “much too much overwriting”: Leven over-romanticises just about everything under the sun and is cursed with a very Irish need to be poetic. His voice is reasonably nice and husky but of limited range, so he cannot give his lines much cadence. Sandlin praises his nimble, Celtic-tinged guitar, for instance in “Me And Angela”, but says one detects the “stench of petty poetasting” fashioned around conventional pop changes. The songs wallow in a mid-tempo trough; dynamics and imaginative instrumentation are forfeited to the lyrics. As specimens of pretentious pseudo-literary writing he cites lines such as “Way back in perfume times” and “Like an animal in prayer”, and on “Deep Choking Wooded Death Fix” he quips, “Ah, big deal, Jacko, John Denver saw it ‘rain fire in the sky’”.

He is kind only to “Empty In Soho Square”, with its violin, whistles and acoustic guitar, one of the few undeniably beautiful pop songs. He also notes that in the liner notes Leven thanks all the bars “for being there the same time as me”, listing about twenty houses of libation. The album sounds as if diary verse had been set to music after a few beers, he says, and would appeal to “45-year old NPR music coordinators”. He ends by hoping Leven will not set the Canterbury Tales to music as a 17-CD box set.

The review contains several factual slips: *Control* is dated 1975 (it was 1971/73), Doll by Doll are called a minor New Wave outfit of the eighties (they were active 1978–82), *The Mystery Of Love* is given as 1995 (UK 1994), and Leven’s name is repeatedly misspelt “Levin”.

undatiert-radio-ffn-nightline-jackie-lev.kurz: A YouTube recording of just over five minutes titled “Call Mother A Lonely Field” from radio ffn’s programme “Nightline”. Date, presenter and content are not documented; the page gives only the title.
inhalt: On YouTube there is an audio recording titled “FFN Nightline 3 Jackie Leven – call mother a lonely field”. It comes from the programme “Nightline” on the Lower Saxony private station radio ffn; the “3” in the title suggests the third part of a multi-part upload. The page carries no description, and the date, presenter and content of the conversation are unknown.

undatiert-songkick-jackie-leven-concert-.kurz: Songkick lists 139 past concerts for Leven from 1992 up to dates in November 2011 overtaken by his death; the database mainly documents his dense touring in 2008-2011.
inhalt: Songkick's artist page "Jackie Leven Tour Dates & Concert History" shows no upcoming dates and 139 past events. The three most recent entries fall in autumn 2011: 30 October at the Kitchen Garden Cafe in Birmingham, 18 November at "Backstage at The Green Hotel" in Kinross and 27 November at the Foyer Bar of the Assembly Hall in Tunbridge Wells; the last two fell after Leven's death on 14 November. The tour leg before that: 22 October Manchester Academy 3, 23 October Trades Club in Hebden Bridge, 24 October York (with John Foxx and the Maths), 27 October The Flowerpot in Derby; before that Bergen (Garage, 14 October), Oslo (John Dee, 7 October), Amsterdam (Paradiso, 2 October) and in September Hamburg, Kiel, Isernhagen, Essen and Munich.

In the full list, by a count of the three-page gigography (136 of the 139 entries usable), there are roughly 30 dates in 2008, about 10 in 2009, about 43 in 2010 and about 31 in 2011; before that only a few entries, for example 1992 (Feltham, London Borderline), 1994, and about 18 together from 1997 to 2007. About three-quarters of the shows are in the United Kingdom (including repeat visits to Union Chapel in London, Winchester, Whitstable, Kinross and Sheffield), about 18 in Germany (Essen, Stuttgart, Dresden, Munich among them), plus Norway, the Netherlands, Sweden, Austria, Switzerland and Canada. The database also includes festivals such as Wickham 2011, the Edge Festival in Edinburgh and HowTheLightGetsIn in Hay-on-Wye. Songkick entries document announcements and user input, not necessarily concerts that took place; the figures give a rough picture of touring density, not a complete chronicle.

undatiert-stv-artery-jackie-leven-dokume.autor: STV (editorial team unknown); upload by Ian Rodgers
undatiert-stv-artery-jackie-leven-dokume.kurz: TV portrait of about 24 minutes, according to the upload description an STV documentary, “ripped from my personal VHS recording” (uploaded 12 September 2018 by Ian Rodgers).
inhalt: TV portrait of about 24 minutes, according to the upload description an STV documentary, “ripped from my personal VHS recording” (uploaded 12 September 2018 by Ian Rodgers). According to the automatic transcript, the opening titles read “Musician – Jackie Leven, the man and his music” and apparently the STV arts magazine “Artery”. Leven speaks at original locations in Fife: on the old railway line in the Leven valley between Leslie and Markinch, where the little steam train stopped in front of his parents' house and showed him that there was life elsewhere; at Ravenscraig Castle near Dysart, where he sat alone as a teenager. He describes Leslie in the 1950s (father Cockney, mother “Romany Geordie”), gang rivalry with the new town of Glenrothes, his mother's blues records and his father's remark about the “screaming black men” in the house, the first guitar at about twelve in Kirkcaldy and his own invented tuning. Then Dorset in the mid-1970s, Doll by Doll from 1977 (“fierce on stage but beautiful on record”), drugs as a result of waiting for tours, an aggressive phase towards the end of the band. In detail: the attack after a night in the studio near Pentonville Road, almost two years without a voice, life in silence, heroin for pain, quitting after a defaced advertising poster of his then girlfriend, acupuncture and “psychic healing”, the founding of the CORE Trust with Princess Diana's support. Finally the return to Scotland's west coast (Kilchurn Castle, Oban), first singing in bars, thoughts on cadence in poetry and song, the press formula “Celtic Soul”. Interspersed are excerpts from “Call Mother a Lonely Field”, “Single Father”, “Marble City Bar” and Doll by Doll material. Tone: a serious, carefully filmed portrait with Leven as the narrator of his own life.

undatiert-taratata-italienisches-tv-jack.kurz: Recording of an appearance on the Italian music show “Taratata” (around 2000, according to the uploader): “Working Man's Love Song” and “Single Father” plus deadpan banter with presenter Gene Gnocchi; uploaded to YouTube in 2007.
inhalt: The YouTube video “Jackie Leven Live on Italian TV” (about 5 min 24 s, uploaded on 30 November 2007 by the channel kennymi5) documents, according to the uploader's description, a live appearance on the late-night Italian music show “Taratata” “around 2000”. It features two songs, “Working Man's Love Song” and “Single Father”, and “typical deadpan Leven verbals” with the comedian presenter Gene Gnocchi. There is nothing beyond this description; the broadcast date and programme name come from the uploader alone, and the conversation has not been transcribed.

undatiert-the-afterword-erwaehnungen-sam.titel: [Overview of mentions: Jackie Leven in other Afterword threads 2015–2026]
undatiert-the-afterword-erwaehnungen-sam.kurz: On the music forum The Afterword Leven keeps cropping up: as the model for refusing encores, as an author of rain songs, as a collector’s artist and as the example of bridge-building between literature and pop (Ian Rankin).
inhalt: A search for “Jackie Leven” on the British music forum The Afterword turns up mentions scattered over years that show how he serves as a fixed point of reference in this community. Some threads are devoted to him, such as the one for what would have been his 65th birthday on 18 June 2015, when a user raises a wee dram and links *Forbidden Songs Of The Dying West*, or for his 72nd birthday in 2022, when fans were invited to meet at “his bench” in Soho Square, London. Another post announces an evening at London’s Betsey Trotwood on 18 November, twelve years after his death, at which Deborah Greenwood (Leven’s wife) and Jinder would celebrate his songs, stories and “all things Levenland”.

Other threads ask where a novice should start, discuss a greatest-hits collection, point to a short documentary on YouTube, and rave about the 4-CD set *Live or Die in Bremen 1999 and 2004* as the best £20 you will spend all year. One list includes the promo CD *Heroes Can Be Any Size: An Introduction to Jackie Leven*, which came free with The Word magazine in March 2012. A user offers duplicate copies of the Leven tribute album.

At the margins Leven is often invoked as a yardstick: in “Encore Etiquette” (14 July 2026) a user prefers the approach of “the late, great Jackie Leven”, who made it clear there would be no encores. In “Scotland – the home of the rain song?” (3 June 2026) “Another Man’s Rain” sits beside songs by Garbage, Eurythmics and John Martyn; a thread of 10 October 2022 notes that Rankin’s book title *A Heart Full of Headstones* comes from “Single Father”. As an example of bridge-building between fiction and popular music, one user writes: “Ian Rankin and Jackie Leven springs to mind.” He also turns up in lists of artists people still buy (“Jackie Leven (until he passed)”) and in gig memories. The tone is consistently admiring.

undatiert-the-list-jackie-leven-lovers-a.kurz: Short review of *Lovers At The Gun Club* in The List: largely positive – songs of redemption and sadness, guest vocals from Johnny Dowd, with only the closing David Childers cover raising a question.
inhalt: The short review, in the singer-songwriter column, describes Kirkcaldy-born Leven as “something of a Celtic/Romany troubadour” returning with his “umpteenth” solo album. The title track opens the record, with guest vocals from his “absinthe-guzzlin’” buddy, the American country star Johnny Dowd. On a number cloned from Willie Dixon, Leven namechecks “a certain English thespian” – “Olivier Blues”.

The songs are primarily about redemption and sadness, casting a shadow as long as Jackie’s 58 years on earth. Other highlights named are “I’ve Passed Away from Human Love” and “The Dent in the Fender and the Wheel of Fate”. The reviewer is left wondering only why Leven and company tacked the Springsteen-esque David Childers song “Heart In My Soul” on at the end. The reference to 58 years points to 2008/09.

undatiert-trouser-press-doll-by-doll.kurz: Ira Robbins reviews Doll by Doll’s four albums and Leven’s solo discography in the Trouser Press Guide: Leven’s voice dominates, *Gypsy Blood* is a peak and *Grand Passion* a failure.
inhalt: The Trouser Press Guide entry, signed by Ira Robbins, is filed under Doll by Doll and lists after it Leven’s complete discography, Concrete Bulletproof Invisible, John St. Field, the work with David Thomas and Ian Rankin, and *Wayside Shrines* (2011). Robbins begins by saying the only constant on Doll by Doll’s four albums is the Scottish singer and guitarist Jackie Leven, who began as leader of a quartet and wound up its only member. On the first three LPs his presence is so commanding, thanks to a deep, rich, expressive voice that leaps into falsetto or descends to an ominous whisper, that everyone around him takes a back seat.

*Remember* he calls an impressive but flawed debut that needlessly limits the band’s obvious electric strength; the folk roots put song before performance, occasionally blunting the excitement – a sophisticated work that mainly introduces Leven’s startling voice. *Revenge of Memory*, which Robbins describes as six long songs cleanly recorded at a Sheffield club show in 1977, runs from soulful (“Chances”) through Who-like guitar improvisation (“More Than Human”) to an uncanny approximation of Elvis Costello (“Sleeping Partners”).

After personnel changes came *Gypsy Blood*: with restraint lifted and emotional intensity cranked up, tunes like “The Human Face” and “Teenage Lightning” are simply magnificent – crystal clear, intricately arranged and full of rock fire – and Leven’s voice and poetic lyrics lend it dramatic grandeur. “A bit overblown, but a real stunner.” The self-titled third album, long delayed by contractual problems, suffers from creeping relaxation: strong songs, but less reach and impact. With vocalist Helen Turner and studio sidemen, Leven attempted something different on *Grand Passion*, and the experiment failed: Turner sings like bad Nico, the lyrics are pretentious and obnoxious, the music adequate but totally unappealing. Robbins dates the band’s last gig to late 1984.

Years later Leven joined former bandmates Jo Shaw and Dave McIntosh in Concrete Bulletproof Invisible, a promising but short-lived quartet with ex-Pistol Glen Matlock; the title track of the *Big Tears* EP lifts its chorus from “White Light/White Heat” but has ideas of its own. Leven then released loads of solo albums, in various combinations and once under a pseudonym, until his death in 2011.
zitate_kontext: Ira Robbins on Jackie Leven in Doll by Doll.

undatiert-waatsveen-no-jackie-leven-et-l.kurz: Extensive memorial page by a Trondheim fan (URL slug “til minne 1950–2011”, last edited on 30 November 2025).
inhalt: Extensive memorial page by a Trondheim fan (URL slug “til minne 1950–2011”, last edited on 30 November 2025). The larger part is a biography in Norwegian compiled from familiar sources: childhood in Fife as a bullied outsider, early fatherhood at 16, Saint Judas recordings for the BBC in 1969, London years, Doll by Doll (Joe Shaw, David McIntosh, Helen Turner; producers and guests such as Tom Newman and David Gilmour), the attack in 1984 with loss of voice and record contract, heroin addiction, CORE Trust and the Diana episode, the solo career from 1994 with pseudonyms and fan-club albums, Ian Rankin and *Jackie Leven Said*, the last concert in Edinburgh in August 2011 and death on 14 November 2011. The author notes that band members and a producer dispute Leven's version of the attack, and calls the Dylan encounter disputed.

Personally: Waatsveen saw Leven live several times, describes him as a great storyteller and warm-hearted person, received signed CDs (dedication “Svein, we are the men”) and reproduces two friendly emails from Leven of 2008 as scans. Asked about his favourite place to play, Leven is said to have named the Polish Club in Kirkcaldy. He lists Norwegian venues (Røros, Stokkøya near Åfjord, Kabelvåg, Bergen, Oslo, Drammen), in Trondheim usually the Credo Bar in autumn; at the Credo concert in 2008 Leven told the story of “The Bonnie Earl of Moray”.

1971-11-06-sounds-take-off-your-head-and.kurz: Still using the name Alan Moffatt, Jackie appears on a 1971 sampler from the Tyneside folk club scene with “Finest Hour”. Jerry Gilbert welcomes the record in *Sounds* as an excellent debut for the new Rubber label.
inhalt: An early trail leads to Newcastle: among the musicians on *Take Off Your Head And Listen*, the first sampler from Rubber Records, is **Alan Moffatt**. His contribution, “Finest Hour”, is marked as a live recording and credits Moffatt as its writer. The label bears ℗ 1971. Jackie had appeared on a record well before *Control*, still using his original name.

Jerry Gilbert introduces the sampler in the folk pages of *Sounds* on 6 November 1971. He praises the debut from the new Newcastle label, its low price and the prospect of further releases by these musicians. His review concerns the compilation as a whole; it offers no separate judgement on Moffatt’s song. The Alan Hull mentioned in the text is the Lindisfarne musician.

The record itself makes the connection visible: “Finest Hour – Alan Moffatt” is the second track on side A. The sleeve thanks the audience at the Rex Hotel Folk/Arts Club; [the Discogs entry for the original pressing](https://www.discogs.com/release/2298445-Various-Take-Off-Your-Head-And-Listen) places the recording at that club and identifies Moffatt as Jackie Leven. [Paul Du Noyer’s obituary](https://www.pauldunoyer.com/the-jackie-leven-obituary/) also gives Alan Moffatt as his original name. The review documents the sampler in autumn 1971, while the label documents his contribution to it.

1972-10-28-nme-john-st-field-folkclubs.titel: The Nationwide Gig Guide [John St Field in the folk clubs]
1972-10-28-nme-john-st-field-folkclubs.autor: John Pidgeon; folk listings: Eric Winter
1972-10-28-nme-john-st-field-folkclubs.kurz: In autumn 1972, John St Field appears among the folk clubs of England’s south coast in the NME gig guide. Two listings pair him with Alex Atterson, whose name is also associated with *Control*.
inhalt: Three small entries in the *New Musical Express* gig guide bring John St Field’s early performing life into focus. For Friday 27 October 1972, the paper lists him with Helen Woodall at the Star Inn in Portsmouth. On Sunday he is due to play with Alex Atterson at the Pembroke Arms in Bournemouth; the following Monday, the two are on the programme at the Blacksmiths Arms in Shirley.

The scale is different from the rock clubs Doll by Doll would later play: three evenings in the folk listings, among many other musicians. Yet **Alex Atterson** is also one of the musicians associated with *Control*. The listings establish that Leven was being advertised as John St Field by October 1972, giving concrete places and dates to an early musical life so often known only through later recollections.

The guide was compiled by John Pidgeon, with Eric Winter credited for the folk listings. Portsmouth appears on printed page 24, Bournemouth and Shirley on page 33. These are announcements rather than concert reports: they do not establish whether the evenings took place as planned or how the musicians performed together.
